rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 29 September 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🟡 The banking industry has extended principal-and-interest repayment relief for individuals affected by the Tai Po fire to end-May 2027. Participating retail banks should sustain eligible-customer servicing, collections handling and mortgage-transition arrangements through that period. • 🟡 The SFC and AFRC have signed a replacement cooperation MoU covering reporting and related audit or assurance work for specified licensed firms and funds. It does not create a new reporting requirement or deadline, but may increase coordination around existing evidence for in-scope entities. Hong Kong 🟡 Banking industry further extends loan repayment grace period for affected individuals of Tai Po Fire 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20260928-hkma-press-2ab80f2940 ⏰ Deadline: End of May 2027 for the further six-month repayment grace period Products: Mortgages, personal loans, credit cards The HKMA and HKAB announced that all 28 retail banks will extend by a further six months, to end-May 2027, the principal-and-interest repayment grace period for affected individuals’ existing mortgages, personal loans and credit-card loans. Wang Fuk Court mortgagee banks will continue to handle mortgages flexibly, including extending the original-mortgage grace period until a newly purchased unit is ready for intake. The announcement is an industry-agreed credit-support measure rather than a new binding HKMA rule. It does not state eligibility evidence, accounting or credit-reporting treatment, fees, or arrangements for SME borrowers. Source: Banking industry further extends loan repayment grace period for affected individuals of Tai Po Fire Primary source: official document 🟡 SFC and AFRC extend regulatory cooperation to financial reporting of licensed firms and funds under new MoU 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20260928-sfc-web-26pr156 ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: Investment services, virtual-asset services The SFC and AFRC signed a new MoU on 28 September 2026, replacing their February 2021 MoU. It covers financial and, where applicable, compliance reporting by licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers, SFC-authorised funds and registered open-ended fund companies, as well as related audit and assurance work. The MoU provides for information sharing, referrals, mutual assistance and coordinated inspections or investigations in matters of mutual regulatory interest, subject to law, and took effect when signed. It is a non-binding statement of intent that does not modify law or create enforceable third-party obligations; its relevance is to existing reporting and audit evidence for entities within the stated scope. Source: SFC and AFRC extend regulatory cooperation to financial reporting of licensed firms and funds under new MoU Primary source: official document SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks.
